hypothesis: The positive funding-carry mechanism observed in FCM-1M can survive costs without collateral exhaustion if exposure is smaller, the isolated futures collateral is much larger, and the short entry basis is reset every month.
mutation_reason: The predecessor had positive stress PnL in every historical window but two modelled futures-collateral exhaustions. This changes risk plumbing only; selection features and thresholds are unchanged. Exactly one allocation/reset variant is tested, with no grid search.

allocation.perpetual_short_quantity: exactly equal base-asset quantity to the spot leg

monthly_rule.decision: First UTC day 00:00 using completed prior-month funding and completed prior daily spot closes only
monthly_rule.execution: Planned at 01:00; both legs atomically use the first common real spot/perpetual hourly open within 168 hours
qualification: last completed spot daily close > EMA50
monthly_rule.selection: highest prior-month funding among qualified assets, deterministic symbol tie-break
monthly_rule.forced_reset: At every monthly requalification close both legs and reopen both legs, even when the selected asset is unchanged; this realizes basis PnL and resets isolated short collateral. No synthetic price may fill an order.

data: Same checksum-verified public anonymous Binance spot 1h, USD-M perpetual 1h, mark-price 1h and funding archives and the same disclosed causal gap hierarchy as FCM-1M; no account, API key or private app data.
historical_gate: Stress net PnL must be positive in every named window, all-available stress must have zero modelled collateral exhaustions, minimum futures equity must remain at least $95 (50% of initial isolated margin), and diagnostic mark leverage must never exceed 1.0x.
promotion_gate: A historical pass authorizes only a frozen paper-forward observation. Live remains disabled until at least 12 prospective months and 12 independent closed monthly episodes are observed with positive stress-adjusted net PnL and measured live basis/costs within assumptions.
limitations: All historical periods were already viewed in related research; none is a genuine untouched holdout.
Maintenance-margin tiers and liquidation-engine mechanics are not simulated; the collateral floor is deliberately stricter than merely remaining above zero.
Exchange default/outage, transfer constraints, taxes, order-book impact and scalable capacity are absent.
Any capital estimate for $25/day is a linear diagnostic extrapolation, not a forecast or promise.
